title: Rigveda 4.49: To Indra and Brihaspati
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.49: To Indra and Brihaspati: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.49 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Indra and Brihaspati. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 308r-308v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>i̱daṁ vā̍m ā̱sye̍ ha̱viḥ pri̱yam i̍ndrābṛhaspatī | u̱ktham mada̍ś ca śasyate ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>DEAR is this offering in your mouth, O Indra and Br̥ihaspati: Famed is the laud, the gladdening draught.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 308r (numbered 117r by the scribe) (OPenn image 308, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.47.4 ‹yajña-vāhasā indravāyūiti ni yacchatam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 308v (numbered 117v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.49.2 ‹-pītaye›. Verse 4.49.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.49.2-6 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 308v
translation.original_text:
2a̱yaṁ vā̱m pari̍ ṣicyate̱ soma̍ indrābṛhaspatī | cāru̱r madā̍ya pī̱taye̍ ||
3ā na̍ indrābṛhaspatī gṛ̱ham indra̍ś ca gacchatam | so̱ma̱pā soma̍pītaye ||
4a̱sme i̍ndrābṛhaspatī ra̱yiṁ dha̍ttaṁ śata̱gvina̍m | aśvā̍vantaṁ saha̱sriṇa̍m ||
5indrā̱bṛha̱spatī̍ va̱yaṁ su̱te gī̱rbhir ha̍vāmahe | a̱sya soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
6soma̍m indrābṛhaspatī̱ piba̍taṁ dā̱śuṣo̍ gṛ̱he | mā̱daye̍thā̱ṁ tado̍kasā ||
translation.text:
2This lovely Soma is effused, O Indra and Br̥ihaspati, For you, to drink it and rejoice.
3As Soma-drinkers to our house come, Indra and Br̥ihaspati-and Indra-to drink Soma juice.
4Vouchsafe us riches hundredfold, O Indra, and Br̥ihaspati, With store of horses, thousandfold.
5O Indra. and Br̥ihaspati, we call you when the meath is shed, With songs, to drink the Soma juice.
6Drink, Indra and Br̥ihaspati, the Soma in the giver's house: Delight yourselves abiding there.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 308v (numbered 117v by the scribe) (OPenn image 309, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.49.2 ‹-pītaye›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 309r (numbered 118r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.50.3 ‹bṛhaspate yā paramā parāvat›. Verses 4.49.2-6 end on this page; 4.49.2 begins on fol. 308r (numbered 117r by the scribe).
